asks: how do I play Aphelios
what does Aphelios want to do
what's my job on Aphelios
Aphelios game plan
how am I supposed to play this champ
say: Farm safely toward items and fight around the two guns you're holding, or swap to the rifle and poke from range if the fight looks bad.
more: You only ever hold two of your five weapons, and each one changes both your basic attack and your ability. The pair in your hands decides what you are good at right now.
Early you are an item-hungry marksman with no dash, so the lane is about farm and not dying. Later the right pair plus Moonlight Vigil can decide a whole fight.
Phase swaps main hand and off hand, so think of it as choosing which attack and which ability you want for the next few seconds.
check: Which two guns you hold, how much ammo each has left, and which gun is next in the queue.
breaks: If you are being dived every fight, stop walking up for damage; stay beside your support and let the fight come to you instead.

when: you are level 6
asks: when is Aphelios strong
what does my ult do at six
should I fight at six on Aphelios
is level six a spike for me
when do I use Moonlight Vigil
say: At six, swap the gun whose effect you want into your main hand before you ult, or hold it for dragon if lane is quiet.
more: Moonlight Vigil explodes on enemy champions and applies whatever your main-hand gun does. The same button is a different ult depending on which gun is out.
That makes Phase part of the ult: swap first, then fire. Firing with the wrong gun in hand wastes most of what the ult could have done.
It hits hardest when their bot lane and jungler stand together, which is exactly what a dragon fight looks like a couple of minutes later.
check: Which gun is in your main hand right now, and whether the enemies are standing close enough together for one blast to catch both.
breaks: If their duo hit six first and you are still five, they have the ult advantage; give the wave and farm under tower until you catch up.

how do I poke in lane as Aphelios
what do I do with the rifle

should I be trading or farming
say: With the rifle out, land the long shot and take the follow-up attack on the mark, or just farm if their support is waiting to engage.
more: Calibrum's ability is a long-range shot that marks whoever it hits, and the mark lets you attack them again from far away. That is poke they cannot answer.
Throw it when they step forward for a last hit, because they are standing still for a moment and the minion they want tells you where they will be.
Chip damage like this is what makes a later all-in or a jungle gank work, so two or three landed shots matter more than they look.
check: Whether the rifle is actually in your main hand, and whether minions are blocking the line to the champion you want to hit.
breaks: If you hold a short-range pair instead, do not walk up to force trades against a longer-range lane; last hit and wait for the rifle to come back around.

say: Before the objective, burn ammo on the wave to cycle toward the pair you want, or keep what you have if the fight starts in seconds.
more: A gun that runs out of ammo goes to the back of the queue and the next one arrives. Spending ammo on minions is how you choose your fight weapons.
The queue slot shows which gun comes next, so you can plan one step ahead: empty the gun you do not want and see what replaces it.
Doing this on a wave also pushes the lane out, which is useful on its own before your team walks to the pit.
check: Ammo left on both guns, which weapon is next in the queue, and how long until the objective actually starts.
breaks: If you would arrive mid-swap with a nearly empty gun, stop cycling; a known pair with ammo beats a perfect pair that shows up late.

who do I hit in fights

say: Stay behind your front line and ult the clump once they commit, or hold the ult and hit whoever dives you if they jump first.
more: You have no dash in your kit, so position is your only defence. Start the fight further back than feels useful and walk forward as their threats get used.
Moonlight Vigil wants several champions close together. The moment after their engage lands is usually when they are bunched up the most.
Hitting the closest safe target is fine. A carry who attacks the tank for the whole fight does more than one who dies reaching for their back line.
check: Where their divers and assassins are standing, and whether their big engage tools have already been used.
breaks: If their team is spread out and poking instead of grouping, do not wait for a perfect ult; use it on the one target your team can kill.

say: Take farm and safe plates now and aim your fights at two or three finished items, or fight sooner if their carry is behind on items.
more: Every gun gets better with items, so each completed item improves all five weapons at once. That is why your curve is steep.
Until then your team is fighting with a weaker carry than theirs might be, so the honest call is often to trade an objective for farm.
Compare items, not kills. If their marksman has one item fewer than you, the spike is already yours and waiting gives it away.
check: The enemy carry's item count against yours on the scoreboard, and whether your team can hold objectives without you for a minute.
breaks: If your team is losing every objective while you farm, the game ends before you scale; group for the next one even if you are one item short.

what does Cho want to do
what's my job on Cho'Gath
Cho'Gath game plan
how do I play this champ
say: Farm and heal off last hits early, then be the huge front line who eats a carry with Feast, or peel your carry if they dive.
more: Carnivore gives you health and mana back for every unit you kill, so you can stay in lane through poke that would send other champions home.
Feast is true damage on one target, and killing with it makes you permanently bigger. Your late game is built out of well-used Feasts.
Rupture and Feral Scream are both area control. You start fights by landing them, or stop fights by landing them on whoever jumps in.
check: How much health Feast would need to finish the target, since the coach cannot see cooldowns or health bars other than yours.
breaks: If you keep missing Rupture, you have no way to reach anyone; stand closer to your team and use it on enemies who come to you.

say: Six is your spike: Feast finishes a low laner and you grow for good, or eat a big minion to grow if no kill is on.
more: Feast deals a large chunk of true damage, so armor and magic resist do nothing against it. A laner who thinks he is safe at low health is not.
It works on any enemy unit and you only grow if it kills. A guaranteed stack on a minion can be better than a risky attempt on a champion.
Each stack is more maximum health forever, which is what lets you stand in front at the dragon and baron fights later.
check: Whether the target is low enough for Feast to kill, and whether Feast is ready.
breaks: If their jungler is alive and has not shown, do not walk past the wave hunting a Feast kill; take the minion stack and keep your lane position.

say: Rupture where they will step for a last hit, then scream and auto with spikes, or just last hit and heal if it keeps missing.
more: Rupture has a delay, so aim at the minion they need rather than at them. The knock-up and slow give you time for the scream and a few attacks.
Feral Scream silences, which means they cannot answer with spells for a moment. That is why the order is knock up first, scream second.
Vorpal Spikes hit everything in front of you and slow, so the same attacks push the wave. Decide whether you want that before you start swinging.
check: Where the wave is, since spikes will push it, and whether you have the mana for the full combo.
breaks: If every missed Rupture gets you poked back for free, stop forcing it; farm with spikes and let Carnivore out-heal the lane.

more: Your passive turns farm into health and mana, so a lane you cannot win can still be a lane you do not lose. Each last hit is a small heal.
A tank who is behind still does his job later, because Rupture, the silence and Feast do not need a gold lead to matter.
Buy against the damage type that is actually hurting you. One early defensive piece often turns their kill threat into nothing.
check: Whether their damage is physical or magic, and whether you can reach the wave without taking a full trade.
breaks: If they are diving you under tower with their jungler, farming there stops being safe; give the wave and ask for help or swap lanes.

say: Stand at the pit and save Feast for the finishing hit on the objective, or spend it on their jungler first if he walks in low.
more: Feast is true damage on any enemy unit, which makes it a second finishing tool next to your jungler's. Two finishers are harder to steal from.
The cost is that Feast is then not available for the fight. If the fight matters more than the objective, eat a champion instead.
Rupture and the silence at the pit entrance keep their jungler off the objective for the seconds that matter.
check: The objective's health and where their jungler is standing, because neither is visible to the coach.
breaks: If their team is already winning the fight around the pit, do not sit waiting for the last hit; use Feast to kill someone or leave.

say: Rupture and scream onto their carries to open the fight, or stand beside your own carry and silence whoever dives if they have more engage.
more: A silence on a mage or an assassin for the first seconds of a fight is often worth more than damage. Aim Feral Scream at whoever relies on spells.
Feast the target that will die to it. A kill grows you mid-fight, so finishing a damaged carry beats chunking a healthy tank.
You are big and slow, so they will see you coming. A Rupture from fog, or onto someone already slowed, is far more reliable than one in the open.
check: Which enemy is the real threat to your carry, and whether your carry is safe enough for you to walk forward.
breaks: If your carries are getting killed behind you while you chase, turn around; a living carry behind a tank wins more fights than a deep Rupture.

what does GP want to do
what's my job on Gangplank
GP game plan
how do I play this champ
say: Farm with Parrrley for the extra gold and scale into barrel fights, or use Cannon Barrage to help another lane while you keep farming yours.
more: Parrrley plunders gold for each unit it kills, so last hitting with it pays more than attacking. Your whole early game is built around that.
Powder Kegs spread your attack's damage to everyone in the blast and slow them. With items behind the attack, one barrel hurts a whole team.
Cannon Barrage is placed on an area rather than on yourself, so it can matter in a fight you are not standing in.
check: Your mana, since Parrrley on every minion runs you dry, and whether anyone is close enough to pop your kegs.
breaks: If you are being run down every time you walk up, drop the greed; last hit with Parrrley from range and give the minions you cannot reach.

say: At six, send Cannon Barrage to a fight in another lane and stay in yours, or keep it for your lane if their jungler shows top.
more: The barrage slows and damages an area, which is enough to turn a two against two or cut off an escape. You help without losing a single minion.
That is your version of roaming. Other top laners have to leave lane to affect the map, and you do not.
Used well around the first dragon fights, it also means your team fights with part of you there while you keep scaling.
check: The minimap for a fight that is starting or an enemy running away, and whether Cannon Barrage is ready.
breaks: If you are being dived or all-inned in your own lane, the ult belongs there; the slow under your tower can save you.

say: Shoot Parrrley at them when they walk up to last hit, or shoot minions for gold instead if they trade back harder than you can afford.
more: Parrrley is ranged, so against a melee laner you can hit without being hit. Against a ranged laner the trade is closer and gold is the safer use.
Your melee attack sets them on fire every few seconds through Trial by Fire. If they step next to you while it is ready, that one hit is a strong trade.
A keg placed near the wave threatens anyone who stands by it. Even when it never explodes, it moves them off the minions.
check: Whether Trial by Fire is ready, how many kegs you have, and your mana.
breaks: If they have a gap closer and jump on you whenever you poke, stop spending Parrrley on them and use it purely to farm from a distance.

Used only as a heal, it leaves you with no answer to the next stun. That is fine when nobody can follow up, and risky otherwise.
Tell yourself which enemy ability you are saving it for before the fight starts, so you are not deciding in the moment.
check: Which enemy ability locks you down, and whether their jungler is alive and could be nearby.

You do the most when the fight comes to a place you prepared, so arriving early at an objective matters more for you than for most.

The side wave you push also drags someone away from the objective, which is the point: they send a player or lose a tower.
The deal only works while your four can stall. If they get engaged on and die in seconds, the slow from far away changes nothing.

how do I play this champ
say: Take short trades early, scale with items, then split push and duel whoever comes, or group and jump their carry if your team needs the fight.
more: Relentless Assault speeds up your attacks the longer you keep hitting, so you get stronger during a fight. Long duels are where you win.
Counter Strike dodges basic attacks and then stuns everyone around you. It decides most of your trades, especially against champions who fight with attacks.
Early you are weaker than you will be, so the lane is about arriving at your items without giving kills away.
check: Whether Counter Strike is ready, because trading without it against an attacker usually loses.
breaks: If your team has no one else to start fights, splitting all game leaves them stuck; group for the important objectives and split in between.

say: From six, long fights favor you because every third hit adds magic damage, or keep trades short if they are a level ahead.
more: Grandmaster-at-Arms makes every third consecutive attack deal extra magic damage. Add your rising attack speed and each second of a duel hurts more.
That flips some matchups. A laner who beat you in short trades can lose once you are allowed to keep attacking.
Levels show on the scoreboard, so check theirs before committing. Being first to six is a real window, and being second is a real danger.
check: Their level compared with yours, and whether Counter Strike is up for the all-in.
breaks: If they can simply walk away or knock you off them, the long fight never happens; take the short trade and wait for more items.

say: Start Counter Strike as they swing at you, then leap on for the stun, or hold it and farm if they mostly fight with spells.
more: Counter Strike dodges incoming attacks for a short time and then stuns everything around you. Starting it just before you leap means you arrive with the stun nearly ready.
Empower your next attack right after the leap so the trade is front-loaded, then walk out while they are stunned.
The dodge works on attacks, not on spells. Against a caster the ability is mostly a stun, so save it for when you can follow up.
check: Whether they fight with basic attacks or abilities, and where the wave is when you leap in.
breaks: If you leap into a big enemy wave, the minions win the trade for them; wait until the wave is even or yours.

how do I lane against this guy
say: Against champions who fight with basic attacks, take long trades inside Counter Strike, or against casters and ranged poke, give CS early and wait for items.
more: Your dodge removes basic attacks entirely for a moment, so a laner whose damage is attacks loses most of his trade while it is active.
Spell damage goes straight through it. Against those champions your leap is the tool: close the gap only when their main ability has been used.
Leap Strike can also jump to a friendly unit, which gives you a way out after a trade when a minion or ally is behind you.
check: What the enemy laner's damage comes from, and whether their key ability was just used.
breaks: If a ranged laner is poking you out before you can leap, do not force it; ask for a gank and farm what the wave gives you near tower.

more: With items, your attack speed and third-hit damage make you very hard to duel. Most single defenders lose to you or have to give the tower.
The goal is to pull numbers away from the objective. If two come for you, your team should be starting dragon or baron four against three.
Leap Strike to a friendly unit is your exit, so keep one in mind before you walk past their tower.
check: Who is missing from the map, and whether you have an escape route before you step up to the tower.
breaks: If your team fights without you and loses four against five, the split was the wrong call; stay closer so you can join the next one.

Going in second, the dodge can blank their marksman for a moment and the stun catches everyone near you.
Peeling is a real option. A stun on the assassin who jumped your carry, followed by your full damage on him, often wins the fight outright.
check: Which of their crowd control abilities have been used, and how far their carry is from their front line.

Counter Strike dodges the monsters' attacks and its stun hits the whole camp, so use it on the camps with several monsters to stay healthy.
Leap plus the stun is a real gank by level three, so you lean toward ganking early more than toward a slow full clear. Six camps still gets you about level four.
check: Which lanes have an enemy pushed far enough forward to gank, and your health after the first buff.

more: Your gank is leap, then stun. Starting Counter Strike before you leap means the stun lands almost as you arrive instead of a moment later.
A lane with its own crowd control doubles that, because their stun covers your approach and yours covers the kill.
Each kill speeds up your items, and you are a champion who gets much stronger with items, so a good early gank is worth more than one camp.

breaks: If the lane is pushed under the enemy tower, the gank needs a dive you are not tanky enough for yet; clear and come back on the next wave.

Kha'Zix game plan

say: Hunt enemies who stand alone, because isolation is your damage, or farm toward your next evolution if everyone is grouped.
more: Unseen Threat marks enemies who are away from their allies, and Taste Their Fear hits much harder on them. One player alone is your whole win condition.
Each rank of Void Assault lets you evolve one ability for good. Your game is a series of upgrades, and farm or kills both get you there.
Against a team that walks together you are weaker, so your job becomes vision, flanks and catching whoever leaves the group first.
check: Whether the target actually shows as isolated before you jump, since a nearby minion or ally changes the damage.
breaks: If they stay grouped all game, stop looking for solo kills; fight with your team and clean up after the first enemy drops.

more: Evolved claws refund part of the cooldown of Taste Their Fear against isolated targets. That is the duelling and pick choice.
Evolved wings make Leap go further and reset it on a kill or assist. That is the teamfight and escape choice.
Level six also gives you invisibility and move speed from Void Assault, which is what makes your ganks hard to react to.
check: What the enemy team looks like: lots of lone targets, or five champions who stay together.
breaks: If you are behind and getting caught, pick the evolution that keeps you alive; a longer leap out is worth more than damage you never get to use.

more: Void Spike heals you when you are inside its explosion, so fire it at monsters next to you. That is what keeps your first clear healthy.
Taste Their Fear does extra damage to a target with nothing beside it, so save it for a lone monster or the last one standing in a camp.

Bot lane has two champions standing together, so your bonus damage is usually missing there. It works when one has recalled or died.
The feed shows who is dead. A support who died seconds ago means their carry is alone for a while, which is your opening.
check: Whether the target is clear of his minions, and whether he still has Flash.

Killing him there costs him camps and tempo and gives you both, which pushes you toward your next evolution faster than farming your own side.
The risk is his lanes collapsing. Go in when the nearest enemy laners are dead, recalled or pinned under their own tower.
check: Which enemy laners are alive and could reach the fight, and which side of the map their jungler was last seen on.

Void Assault makes you invisible and faster, so use it to cross the gap or to drop focus after your first burst.
With evolved wings, a kill or assist gives Leap back. One clean kill can become a second jump, in or out.
check: Who is standing apart from the rest, and whether you have a way out after the kill.

say: Push every wave with Visions and Voidlings so you move first, then lock one target down with your ult, or just farm safely behind your passive.
more: Your spells clear minions quickly, so you can usually shove the wave and be the first mid laner free to help your jungler.

say: With Cultivation of Spirit on, attack minions beside them so the damage spreads, or slow them with the bead and back off if they engage first.
more: While it is active your attacks spread to nearby enemies. You can keep last hitting and still damage a champion standing in his own wave.
Arc of Judgment slows. Used first it sets up a few free attacks, and used second it covers your retreat.
The spreading attacks also push the wave. If you do not want the lane shoved toward their tower, use it in short bursts.
check: Where the enemy stands relative to their minions, and whether you want the wave to push.
breaks: If their support is waiting for you to step forward, spreading attacks from the far side of the wave is enough; do not walk past it.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Yunara
how do I teamfight on Yunara
when do I ult in a fight
who do I hit
where do I stand in fights
say: Hit the nearest target with Cultivation of Spirit on so attacks spread through them, or ult early for the dash if someone dives you.
more: Spreading attacks mean hitting the front line still damages whoever stands behind it. You do not need to reach their carry to hurt him.
The ult turns your speed boost into a dash. Pressing it at the start of the fight is fine if that dash is what keeps you alive.
Stay a step behind your front line and move forward only as their engage tools are spent.
check: Where their divers are, and whether your ult and Cultivation of Spirit are both ready.
breaks: If the enemies are spread wide, the spreading attacks do little; focus one target with your team instead.

when: you have fewer than two completed items
asks: does Yunara scale
when do I get strong on Yunara
should I farm or fight right now
how long until I can carry
am I weak early
say: Farm safely and take plates when it's free, aiming fights at two crit items, or join an early dragon fight if your team already outnumbers them.
more: Your passive needs critical strikes to do anything, so before your crit items you are missing part of your kit. That is why early fights feel weak.
Each crit item adds physical and magic damage at once. The jump from one item to two is bigger for you than for most carries.
The feed shows who is dead. An enemy down before an objective makes it a safe fight even on few items.
check: Your finished items against their carry's, and how many enemies are alive when a fight is called.
breaks: If your team keeps losing objectives while you farm, come to the next one anyway and attack from the back.
